text: Let's go back to that plastic bag.
It wasn't alone. On those dives, explorers also spotted candy wrappers near the bottom.
And in 2019, scientists led by deep-sea biologist Alan Jamieson went looking inside those amphipods from the deepest trenches on Earth, including the Mariana.
They found tiny pieces of plastic and synthetic fibres in their guts. In the Mariana Trench samples... every single one they checked had eaten them.
[sad, small voice now] I thought it was dinner.
[quiet, taking off his goggles] Eleven kilometres down. In a place almost no human has seen.
Plastic sinks slowly. It drifts. It breaks into smaller and smaller pieces. And the trench, like a giant funnel, collects what falls.
The deepest place on our planet. And it already has our fingerprints on it.
